title: A slightly wider tiny tube
hook: Change tube radius and predict laminar volume-flow rate.
misconception: laminar volume-flow rate doubles when tube radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL) to compare laminar volume-flow rate when tube radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With ideal Poiseuille flow with fixed pressure drop viscosity and length, Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL). When tube radius doubles, laminar volume-flow rate becomes 16 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL); scaling exponent 4. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider ideal Poiseuille flow with fixed pressure drop viscosity and length, with a nonzero initial result. If tube radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on laminar volume-flow rate?
recall.why: Apply Q = πΔPr⁴/(8ηL) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 81.
